examples.en: I have known that person for a long time.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 교분이 두터워서 자주 만나요.
examples.en: The two have a close bond, so they meet often.
I went to the gathering to build relationships.
I don't really have any acquaintance with that person.

examples.ko: 학교 선배와의 교분 덕분에 일자리를 구했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my ties with a school senior, I found a job.

examples.ko: 교분이 깊어질수록 서로 더 믿게 됐어요.
examples.en: The deeper our relationship got, the more we trusted each other.

explain: '우정'보다 서로 알고 사귀며 지내는 사이를 말하는 느낌이고 조금 격식 있는 말이에요. '교분이 있다/두텁다/깊다', '교분을 쌓다'처럼 써요. 평소에는 '알고 지내요', '친해요'라고 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I built up a friendship with him over a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간을 들여 알고 지내는 사이를 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means building an acquaintance over time.

phrases.en: The two families have close ties.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랫동안 가깝게 지낸 사이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the relationship is long and close.

phrases.en: I have no acquaintance with that person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 알고 지내는 사이가 아니라는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says the two people don't know each other.

explain_en: Deep personal ties built over time, a bit formal (교분을 쌓다) Rather than friendship itself, it describes a relationship of knowing and associating with someone, in a somewhat formal tone. It is used as '교분이 있다/두텁다/깊다' and '교분을 쌓다'. In daily speech people more often say '알고 지내요' or '친해요'.

en: to return a favor; to reciprocate

examples.ko: 비싼 선물을 받으면 답례해야 할 것 같아서 부담이 커요.
examples.en: When I get an expensive gift, I feel I should return the favor, so it's a burden.

examples.ko: 선물을 받았으니 저도 답례를 해야 할 것 같아요.
examples.en: I got a gift, so I think I should give something back too.

examples.ko: 도와주신 분께 작은 선물로 답례하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to thank the person who helped me with a small gift.
How should we repay the guests when they come?

examples.ko: 친구가 밥을 사 줘서 제가 커피로 답례했어요.
examples.en: My friend bought me a meal, so I returned the favor with coffee.

examples.ko: 작은 떡을 돌려서 이웃에게 답례하는 사람도 많아요.
examples.en: Many people also thank their neighbors by handing out small rice cakes.

explain: 받은 호의나 선물에 대한 보답으로 무엇을 돌려줄 때 써요. '보답하다'가 더 넓게 쓰이고, '답례하다'는 선물이나 인사처럼 구체적인 것을 돌려주는 느낌이에요. 명사 '답례'는 '답례품'으로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: We gave a thank-you gift to the wedding guests.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감사의 뜻으로 돌려주는 선물을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a gift given back as thanks.

phrases.en: I'll buy you dinner in return for your help.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받은 도움을 갚는 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give the reason as repaying help received.

phrases.en: I really want to repay your kindness.
phrases.nuance_ko: '답례하다'보다 넓게 쓰고, 마음이나 행동으로 갚는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than '답례하다', with a feeling of repaying through heart or action.

explain_en: Use it when you give something back in return for a kindness or gift. '보답하다' is broader, while 답례하다 feels like returning something concrete, such as a gift or a greeting. The noun 답례 is also often used as '답례품' (a return gift).

t90.ax: How should we repay the guests when they come?

examples.en: A benefactor donated a scholarship to the school.

examples.ko: 익명의 독지가 덕분에 도서관이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: Thanks to an anonymous benefactor, a new library was built.

examples.ko: 독지가들의 도움으로 아이들이 따뜻한 겨울을 보내요.
examples.en: With help from benefactors, the children spend a warm winter.
The benefactor's good deed was featured in the news.

examples.ko: 이 병원은 독지가에게 받은 후원금으로 운영돼요.
examples.en: This hospital runs on donations from a benefactor.
There was a notice posted saying they were looking for a benefactor.

explain: 어려운 사람이나 단체를 도우려고 돈을 내놓는 고마운 사람을 높여 부르는 말이에요. 뉴스나 기사에서 많이 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '기부하신 분', '후원자'라고 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: Thanks to a benefactor's help, the children received books.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기부 덕분에 생긴 일을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for things that happened thanks to a donation.

phrases.example: 마을에 독지가가 나타나 다리를 놓아 줬어요.
phrases.en: A benefactor appeared in the village and built a bridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도와줄 사람이 뜻밖에 생겼다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense that a helper unexpectedly appeared.

phrases.example: 후원자 덕분에 행사를 열 수 있었어요.
phrases.en: Thanks to a sponsor, we could hold the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, and more common in everyday talk.

explain_en: It respectfully refers to a generous person who gives money to help people in need or an organization. You see it often in news and articles, while in daily talk people more often say '기부하신 분' or '후원자'.

t90.ax: A benefactor donated a scholarship to the school.

examples.en: I don't want to burden my friend with the work.
You must not make the customers bear the cost.
The company made employees pay for training.
They put too much on the child.
I'm sorry, it feels like I'm putting a load on you.
We can't place the caregiving burden on the family.

explain: '부담시키다'는 남에게 짐이나 비용을 지게 한다는 뜻이라 조금 딱딱해요. 대화에서는 '부담을 주다'를 더 자주 써요. 비용은 '~에게 비용을 부담시키다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I don't want to be a burden to my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서는 '부담시키다'보다 이 말을 더 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is used more than '부담시키다' in conversation.

phrases.en: I'm sorry to burden you, teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 정중하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used politely toward someone senior.

phrases.en: We don't make customers pay the cost.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비용이나 짐을 지우지 않는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means not putting the cost or load on someone.

explain_en: 부담시키다 means making another person carry a load or cost, and it sounds a bit stiff. In conversation 부담을 주다 is more common. For costs you say '~에게 비용을 부담시키다'.

examples.en: Grandmother took good care of her grandson.

examples.ko: 남편이 아내를 살뜰히 챙기는 모습이 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: It's nice to see the husband look after his wife so attentively.
I carefully saved my allowance and bought a gift.

examples.ko: 새로 온 직원을 살뜰히 가르쳐 줬어요.
examples.en: I patiently taught the new employee.
That shop welcomes customers warmly.
The teacher looks after each student with care.

explain: '살뜰하다'의 부사형으로 '살뜰히 챙기다, 돌보다, 가르치다'처럼 사람을 정성껏 대하는 동작과 잘 어울려요. 돈을 아끼는 이야기에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: My friend helped with my work very attentively.
phrases.nuance_ko: '살뜰히'와 뜻이 같고, '하게' 모양이라 말할 때 조금 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '살뜰히', and the '-게' form often sounds more natural in speech.

phrases.en: Mom packed my lunchbox with great care.
phrases.nuance_ko: '살뜰히'는 세심하게 챙기는 느낌이고 '정성껏'은 온 마음을 다하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '살뜰히' feels attentive, while '정성껏' feels wholehearted.

phrases.en: She runs her household with careful attention.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집안일을 알뜰하고 정성스럽게 하는 모습에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits someone who manages the home frugally and with care.

explain_en: Caring and frugal in managing household or family needs (살뜰히 챙기다). This is the adverb form of '살뜰하다' and goes well with actions of caring for people, like '살뜰히 챙기다', '돌보다' and '가르치다'. It can also be used when talking about saving money.

examples.en: When the customer arrived, the staff member greeted them politely.
I learned how to turn down a request politely.
He explained the reason he was late in a courteous way.

examples.ko: 선생님께 정중히 여쭤봤더니 친절하게 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: When I asked the teacher respectfully, they kindly told me.
I formally asked them to attend the meeting.

examples.ko: 실수를 정중히 사과했지만 상대는 아직 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I apologized politely for the mistake, but the other person was still angry.

explain: 말과 태도를 예의 바르고 신중하게 한다는 뜻의 부사예요. '사과하다, 거절하다, 부탁하다, 인사하다'처럼 사람 사이의 행동과 잘 어울려요. '공손히'보다 격식 있는 자리나 공적인 상황에 더 잘 맞고, 일상에서는 '예의 바르게'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I politely showed the customer the way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정중히와 뜻이 같고 일상 대화에서 더 흔하게 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 정중히, and the more common form in daily speech.

phrases.example: 그 직원은 항상 정중한 태도로 말해요.
phrases.en: That employee always speaks in a polite manner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸미는 형용사 모양으로 바꿔 쓸 때예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form, used to describe a noun.

phrases.example: 아이가 두 손으로 공손히 선물을 받았어요.
phrases.en: The child politely received the gift with both hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이지만 격식보다 예의 바른 몸짓에 더 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, fitting respectful gestures more than formality.

explain_en: This adverb means doing something in a courteous and careful way, and it pairs well with verbs of interaction like apologizing, refusing, asking and greeting. It fits formal or public situations better than '공손히'. In daily talk people also say '예의 바르게'.

examples.en: Despite the teacher's repeated pleas, the students came late.
I haven't forgotten my mother's earnest request.
After much earnest begging, I finally got a promise.

examples.ko: 친구는 비밀로 해 달라고 신신당부를 했어요.
examples.en: My friend earnestly begged me to keep it secret.
Even though I'd been told repeatedly, I made a mistake again.
Thanks to my father's repeated warnings, I went carefully.

explain: 몇 번이고 간곡하게 부탁하거나 당부하는 일이에요. '신신당부를 하다'처럼 쓰고, 보통 걱정되거나 꼭 지켜야 하는 일을 말할 때 나와요.

phrases.en: My mother earnestly told me to be careful on the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '당부하는 사람'의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Told from the side of the person making the plea.

phrases.en: I heard the doctor's earnest request.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음을 다해 정성스럽게 하는 부탁이라는 뜻의 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar phrase for a request made sincerely.

phrases.en: I received earnest instructions from my grandmother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 거듭 부탁을 받았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an elder repeatedly asked you to do something.

explain_en: It means asking or urging someone earnestly, again and again. It is used as '신신당부를 하다', typically about something worrying or something that must be kept.

en: to bear in mind; to pay heed

examples.ko: 계약 조건은 서명하기 전에 꼭 유념해 두세요.
examples.en: Please be sure to keep the contract terms in mind before signing.

examples.ko: 어린이 보호 구역에서는 속도를 줄여야 한다는 점을 늘 유념하며 운전해요.
examples.en: I always drive keeping in mind that I must slow down in school zones.

examples.ko: 약은 식후에 먹어야 한다는 점을 유념하세요.
examples.en: Please keep in mind that you should take this medicine after meals.
I'll keep that point in mind from now on.

examples.ko: 이번 일을 계기로 안전 수칙에 더 유념했어요.
examples.en: After this incident, I paid more attention to the safety rules.

examples.ko: 유념하지 않으면 같은 실수를 되풀이할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't keep it in mind, you may repeat the same mistake.

explain: '~점을 유념하다', '~에 유념하다'처럼 쓰고, 주의할 것을 마음에 두고 신경 쓴다는 느낌이에요. '명심하다'는 깊이 새긴다는 느낌이 더 강하고, '유념하세요'는 안내문이나 당부하는 말에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: Please keep the entry hours in mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 부탁하는 말에서 자주 들리는 높임 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite expression often heard in notices and requests.

phrases.en: I'll keep my teacher's words firmly in mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유념하다'보다 깊이 새긴다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels stronger than '유념하다', as if engraving it in your mind.

phrases.example: 이 규칙을 유념해 두면 실수가 줄어요.
phrases.en: If you keep this rule in mind, you'll make fewer mistakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 두다'를 붙여 미리 마음에 담아 둔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 두다' means to keep something in mind ahead of time.
phrases.en_equiv: to keep in mind in advance

explain_en: Formal request to pay attention, used in notices (유념해 주세요) It is used as '~점을 유념하다' or '~에 유념하다', meaning to keep something to be careful about in mind. '명심하다' feels stronger, as if engraving it deep in your mind, and '유념하세요' is often heard in notices and cautions.

t90.ax: I'll keep that point in mind from now on.

examples.ko: 인쇄물은 회의 전에 미리 나눠 주세요.
examples.en: Please hand out the printouts before the meeting.
There was a typo in the printout, so I printed it again.

examples.ko: 이 인쇄물을 열 장 복사해 주시겠어요?
examples.en: Could you make ten copies of this printout?
I received an information handout at the entrance of the event.
I have a lot of printed material, so my bag is heavy.

examples.ko: 종이 인쇄물 대신 파일로 보내 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll send it as a file instead of a paper printout.

explain: 회사나 학교에서 말할 때는 보통 '프린트'라고 더 편하게 해요. '프린트 좀 나눠 주세요'는 일상 말투이고, '인쇄물'은 공지나 서류에서 써요. 책, 전단지, 포스터까지 넓게 가리킬 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Could you hand out the printouts?
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 학교에서 '인쇄물'보다 편하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: At work or school it is a more casual word than 인쇄물.

phrases.en: I received the event printout at the entrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이로 된 자료를 받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you receive materials on paper.

phrases.en: I received a promotional flyer on the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고나 안내를 위해 만든 종이를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to paper made for advertising or information.

explain_en: At work or school people casually say '프린트'. '프린트 좀 나눠 주세요' is everyday speech, while '인쇄물' fits notices and documents. It can broadly cover books, flyers, and posters too.

examples.ko: 아버지가 세계 문학 전집을 사 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father bought me a complete collection of world literature.

examples.ko: 그 작가의 전집이 드디어 다 나왔어요.
examples.en: The complete works of that author have finally all come out.
I borrowed a full set of fairy tales from the library.

examples.ko: 전집으로 사면 한 권씩 사는 것보다 싸요.
examples.en: Buying the whole set is cheaper than buying one book at a time.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 읽던 전집이 아직 책장에 있어요.
examples.en: The book set I read as a kid is still on the shelf.

examples.ko: 이 전집은 열 권으로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This collection consists of ten volumes.

explain: 한 작가의 작품이나 한 주제의 책을 세트로 묶은 것이에요. 한 권씩 따로 파는 '낱권'과 반대되고, 어린이 책이나 세계 문학처럼 '동화 전집', '○○ 전집'으로 많이 불러요.

phrases.en: I bought a complete set of fairy tales for my child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린이 책 세트를 말할 때 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common phrase for a set of children's books.

phrases.en: I bought the complete works of my favorite writer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책을 세트로 구입할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the pairing used when buying books as a set.

phrases.example: 전집이 비싸서 낱권으로 한 권만 샀어요.
phrases.en: The full set was expensive, so I bought just one single volume.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전집의 반대로, 책을 한 권씩 따로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 전집, used for books taken one volume at a time.

explain_en: A book series sold or kept as a full set. It is a set of books bundled together, either by one author or one theme. It is the opposite of buying single volumes ('낱권'), and is commonly used in names like '동화 전집' or '○○ 전집', especially for children's books and world literature.

examples.en: I truly think of you as a friend.
I want to express my sincere gratitude.
If that is really true, it's a serious matter.
It was such a truly beautiful view that I gazed at it for a long time.

examples.ko: 진실로 사랑하는 사람에게는 거짓말을 못 해요.
examples.en: You can't lie to someone you truly love.
I was truly impressed by his effort.

explain: 편지나 연설, 글처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 '정말로'의 뜻으로 써요. 평소 대화에서는 '정말', '진짜'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I sincerely congratulate you.
phrases.nuance_ko: '진실로'처럼 마음을 담은 표현이지만 말할 때도 자연스러워요. 감사, 축하, 사과와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like '진실로' it expresses sincerity, but it is natural in speech too, especially with thanks, congratulations and apologies.

phrases.en: I'm really thankful.
phrases.nuance_ko: '진실로'보다 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is much more natural in everyday conversation than '진실로'.

phrases.en: I truly apologize.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거짓 없는 마음을 강조할 때 써요. '진실로'처럼 조금 격식 있게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It stresses a genuine heart and sounds somewhat formal, like '진실로'.

explain_en: Formal, heartfelt; used with thanks or apology (진실로 감사드립니다) It means 'really' in formal settings such as letters, speeches and writing. In everyday conversation '정말' or '진짜' sounds much more natural.

t90.ax: I truly think of you as a friend.

examples.en: The desks in the library have dividers.

examples.ko: 칸막이를 세워서 방을 두 개로 나눴어요.
examples.en: I put up a partition and divided the room into two.

examples.ko: 칸막이 너머에서 옆 사람 목소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear the neighbor's voice from beyond the partition.
I stuck a family photo on my office partition.
I organized the drawer by adding dividers inside.
The partition makes the room look small.

explain: 사무실, 도서관, 식당, 화장실에서 자주 보는 공간을 나누는 얇은 벽이나 판이에요. '벽'은 건물을 이루는 단단한 것이고 '칸막이'는 세우거나 옮길 수 있는 가벼운 것이에요. 서랍을 나누는 판도 '칸막이'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I put up a partition in the middle of the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공간을 나누려고 가볍게 세울 때 '치다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '치다' is used for putting up a light divider to split a space.

phrases.en: When I sit in a partitioned seat, I can focus well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도서관이나 식당에서 가려진 자리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a screened-off seat in libraries or restaurants.

phrases.example: 서랍 칸막이 덕분에 양말을 정리하기 쉬워요.
phrases.en: Thanks to the drawer divider, it's easy to organize socks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서랍 안을 나누는 작은 판을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the small panel that divides a drawer.

explain_en: It is a thin wall or board that divides space, often seen in offices, libraries, restaurants, and restrooms. A '벽' is a solid part of a building, while a '칸막이' is lighter and can be set up or moved. The panels that divide a drawer are also '칸막이'.

examples.en: I wrote a card wishing our teacher a speedy recovery.

examples.ko: 며느리는 시어머니의 쾌유를 빌며 약을 정성껏 달였어요.
examples.en: The daughter-in-law carefully brewed the medicine, praying for her mother-in-law's recovery.

examples.ko: 친구가 입원해서 쾌유를 기원하는 꽃을 보냈어요.
examples.en: My friend was hospitalized, so I sent flowers wishing a quick recovery.

examples.ko: 다친 선수에게 팬들이 쾌유 메시지를 남겼어요.
examples.en: Fans left get-well messages for the injured player.

examples.ko: 할아버지의 쾌유를 위해 온 가족이 기도했어요.
examples.en: The whole family prayed for Grandpa's recovery.
I wish you a quick recovery.

explain: 주로 아픈 사람에게 카드나 메시지로 '빠른 쾌유를 빕니다'처럼 정중하게 인사할 때 써요. 가까운 친구에게는 '빨리 나아'라고 편하게 말해요. 보통 '쾌유를 빌다/바라다/기원하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I hope you get well soon; I wish you a full recovery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아픈 사람에게 정중하게 마음을 전하는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common polite way to send good wishes to someone ill.

phrases.en: All the staff wished the president a full recovery.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빌다'보다 격식 있는 말이라 편지나 공식 글에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: More formal than '빌다', suited to letters and official writing.

phrases.en: I wish you a speedy recovery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카드나 메시지에서 '빠른'을 앞에 붙여 인사말로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '빠른' placed in front is typical of greeting cards and messages.

explain_en: It is mainly used in cards and messages to a sick person, politely, as in '빠른 쾌유를 빕니다'. To a close friend, people say '빨리 나아' more casually. It usually appears as '쾌유를 빌다/바라다/기원하다'.

en: to be willing and cheerful; to be hearty

examples.ko: 그 배우는 인터뷰 요청에 흔쾌히 응했어요.
examples.en: The actor readily agreed to the interview request.
When I asked, my senior gladly said yes.

examples.ko: 아버지께서 여행을 흔쾌히 허락해 주셔서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that my father gladly allowed the trip.
I felt relieved hearing the cheerful, willing answer.

examples.ko: 친구가 이사를 도와 달라는 말에 흔쾌히 그러자고 했어요.
examples.en: My friend gladly said yes when I asked for help moving.

examples.ko: 그는 모든 비용을 흔쾌하게 내겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: He said he would gladly pay all the costs.

explain: 주로 '흔쾌히'로 쓰고, '응하다·승낙하다·허락하다' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 상대의 부탁이나 제안을 망설임 없이 기쁘게 받아들이는 태도를 말해요. 비슷한 '기꺼이'는 일상에서 더 편하게 쓰고, 반대 느낌은 '마지못해'예요.

phrases.en: The boss happily agreed to my request.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흔쾌히'는 '흔쾌하다'의 부사형으로, 망설임 없이 받아들일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '흔쾌히' is the adverb form, used when accepting without hesitation.

phrases.en: I felt good hearing such a willing answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기쁘게 받아들이는 대답을 '흔쾌한'으로 꾸며 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes an answer given with a willing, cheerful attitude.

phrases.en: If you ask for help, I'll gladly help.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흔쾌히'와 뜻이 비슷하고 일상에서 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to '흔쾌히' and more casual in daily speech.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '흔쾌히' and pairs well with verbs like 응하다, 승낙하다 and 허락하다. It describes accepting a request or offer willingly, without hesitation. '기꺼이' is a similar and more casual word, and the opposite feel is '마지못해' (reluctantly).

t90.ax: When I asked, my senior gladly said yes.
